capabilities: Extract text, LaTeX math, and tables from images and PDFs into Markdown
Generate structured descriptions of charts, diagrams, and infographics
OCR images pasted from the clipboard at the cursor via hotkey
Run inference locally through llama.cpp or Ollama, or via the Hugging Face API
Downscale images and configure presets to fit low-VRAM GPUs
disambiguation: Not only a text-transcription tool; it can also turn charts, plots, and diagrams into structured written descriptions.
extras: Desktop-only plugin (isDesktopOnly: true); the README documents shell execution and filesystem access under Obsidian Developer Policies. GLM-OCR GGUF weights (~1 GB total) must be downloaded separately for local use.
intentEvidence: Based on and inspired by the original obsidian-latex-ocr by lucasvanmol.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to convert images, screenshots, or scanned PDFs into editable Markdown, LaTeX math, or tables.

relations.evidence: Based on and inspired by the original obsidian-latex-ocr by lucasvanmol.
Ollama: Connects to your local Ollama instance with auto-start support.
llama.cpp: Native, blazing-fast GGUF execution with optional GPU offloading.
Hugging Face API: Free cloud inference with zero local dependencies or GPU requirements.

summary: Multimodal OCR plugin that extracts text, LaTeX formulas, and tables from images and PDFs using local VLMs or the Hugging Face API.
